Construction sequence of a strutted diaphragm-wall excavation

The crane lifts out the excavator, and the blinding concrete and the reinforced concrete base slab are cast. Then the basement levels are built; as the floor slabs are completed, the struts are removed from the bottom upwards.
With the last cut the pit reaches the design foundation level. The excavated soil is lifted out by the crane between the struts.
Excavation to final level
The lowest strut level carries the largest force: earth pressure increases with depth.
Strut level 3
The pit is now deepening in the impermeable clay: no water enters from below either, because the wall is keyed into the impermeable layer.
Excavation below strut level 3
Waling beam, tubular strut, preloading – just as above.
Strut level 2
The next cut reaches below the second strut level. Below the water table the water enclosed by the walls is pumped out – outside, the groundwater stays where it is.
Excavation below strut level 2
A steel waling beam is fixed to the walls, the crane lifts the tubular strut into place, and it is preloaded with a jack. Only then may excavation continue.
Strut level 1
The soil is excavated only slightly below the first strut level: until then the wall stands as a cantilever, held by its embedment.
Excavation below strut level 1
A reinforced concrete capping beam ties the tops of the panels together. The wall is complete over its full depth and keyed into the impermeable clay – only now does excavation begin.
The diaphragm wall is complete
On the opposite side the diaphragm wall is built in the same way, panel by panel. The wall encloses the excavation before a single spadeful of soil is removed from it.
The opposite wall
Concrete is placed from the bottom upwards through a tremie pipe: the heavier concrete displaces the bentonite slurry, which is returned to the mixing plant.
Concreting from the bottom
The crane lowers the reinforcement cage into the slurry-filled trench.
The grab excavates the trench to the design depth, into the impermeable clay. The excavated soil is continuously replaced by bentonite slurry, which supports the sides of the trench.
Trench excavation under bentonite slurry
First a pair of reinforced concrete guide walls, 1.0–1.5 m high, is built on both sides of the trench: they guide the grab and support the loose upper soil.
